{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfQbH81Yh6nxQ6u1jBHCR","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I made `op_distort_tanh` faster on AVX2: about 1.07–1.10x in two runs of the short benchmark (42.3 → 38.5 and 41.7 → 38.9 ns/block). The check passed the allowlist, build and fixed-stimulus checks, and the tanh approximation's error measured −114.9 dBFS, under the −100 dBFS limit. `op_distort_soft` measured 0.99x both times. Its code is unchanged, so I read that as noise, but the full benchmark will decide. The hidden stimuli, unit suites and longer benchmark only run at final verification, so they haven't been run yet.\n\n**What was slow:** the tanh kernel was limited by the two floating-point ports, with about 20 operations per 8 samples on them. `op_distort_soft` spends its time on two exact divisions per 8 samples. It has to stay bit-identical, so neither division can be replaced, and I left it alone.\n\n**The change** (only `tanh_approx_avx2` in `cedar/include/cedar/opcodes/distortion.hpp`):\n- **Magnitude and sign:** the kernel works on |y| and puts the sign back with and/xor. The clamp is now one `max` instead of `min` + `max`, and the bit operations can run on the third port.\n- **Table lookup:** e^(−2|y|) is split into 2^(k/8) × 2^f. The 2^(j/8) part comes from an 8-entry table read with `vpermps`, which also runs on the third port. The integer offset is folded into the table entries, so one integer add both cancels it and sets the exponent.\n- **Smaller polynomial:** with |f| ≤ 1/16, a quadratic for 2^f is enough (relative error < 3.5e-6), replacing the old degree-4 one.
